enonce_intro_markdown:
The grouped ages, in years, of 50 students in a certain professional institution are shown below.

| Age (years) | 16 - 20 | 21 - 25 | 26 - 30 | 31 - 35 | 36 - 40 | 41 - 45 | 46 - 50 | 51 - 55 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency ($f$) | 5 | 10 | 15 | 9 | 5 | 3 | 2 | 1 |

figures.legende: Cumulative frequency curve (ogive) of the ages of the 50 students, with the median read at cumulative frequency 25 (model answer to Q2(c) and (d)).

incertitudes: Question 2 : le sujet ne dit pas que les âges sont arrondis à l'année ; c'est l'hypothèse retenue (classe 16 - 20 = $15.5 \le x < 20.5$, frontières 15.5, 20.5, ..., 55.5, centres de classe 18, 23, ..., 53), comme pour tout tableau de données groupées de ce type dans cette série.

Question 2 (b) : l'écart type est calculé avec le diviseur $n = 50$ (écart type de la distribution groupée) : $\sigma = 8.19$ ; avec le diviseur $n - 1$ on obtiendrait $s = 8.27$. Le diviseur $n$ est la convention des formulaires du GCE Board utilisée dans les autres sujets du lot.

Question 2 (c) et (d) : le tracé est à faire par l'élève ; le corrigé donne le tableau des fréquences cumulées et une figure modèle (PNG tracé par script, pas figure imprimée du sujet). La médiane est lue à la fréquence cumulée $\frac{n}{2} = 25$ : lecture graphique d'environ 28.7 à 28.9, interpolation linéaire exacte 28.83.
Question 2 : les points imprimés par partie, 3, 4, 4 et 2, totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Calculate the mean age of the students.
(b) Find, to 2 decimal places, the standard deviation of the students' ages.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The standard deviation of a grouped distribution is $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f} - \bar{x}^2}$. Using the totals of the table in part (a):

$$\sigma^2 = \frac{48655}{50} - (30.1)^2 = 973.1 - 906.01 = 67.09$$

$$\sigma = \sqrt{67.09} = 8.1908\ldots$$

**Standard deviation $= 8.19$ years** (to 2 decimal places).

(With divisor $n - 1 = 49$, the sample standard deviation would be $s = \sqrt{\frac{50}{49} \times 67.09} = 8.27$; the formula with divisor $n$ is the one used here.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Draw a cumulative frequency curve for these data.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ages are given to the nearest year, so the class $16 - 20$ really covers $15.5 \le \text{age} < 20.5$; the class boundaries are $15.5,\ 20.5,\ \ldots,\ 55.5$. A cumulative frequency is attached to each **upper** class boundary, and the curve starts at $(15.5, 0)$.

| Age less than (years) | 15.5 | 20.5 | 25.5 | 30.5 | 35.5 | 40.5 | 45.5 | 50.5 | 55.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 5 | 15 | 30 | 39 | 44 | 47 | 49 | 50 |

**To draw the curve:** take the age (years) on the horizontal axis, e.g. 2 cm for 5 years from 15.5 to 55.5, and the cumulative frequency on the vertical axis, e.g. 2 cm for 10 students from 0 to 50. Plot the nine points $(15.5, 0), (20.5, 5), (25.5, 15), \ldots, (55.5, 50)$, label both axes and join the points with a smooth S-shaped curve (the ogive). The curve is steepest between $25.5$ and $30.5$, where the class frequency ($15$) is largest.

![fig-1](gce-al-pm-statistics-2026-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) From the curve, estimate the median age of the students.
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $n = 50$ the median corresponds to the cumulative frequency $\dfrac{n}{2} = 25$. Read across from $25$ on the vertical axis to the curve, then down to the horizontal axis (dashed lines in the figure above): the median is about $28.8$ years.

Check by linear interpolation in the class $25.5 - 30.5$ (cumulative frequency $15$ at $25.5$ and $30$ at $30.5$):

$$\text{Median} = 25.5 + \frac{25 - 15}{30 - 15} \times 5 = 25.5 + 3.33 = 28.83$$

**The median age is about $28.8$ years** (any graphical reading close to $28.8$ is acceptable).
